page.layout: One page of running text in one column. The running head is at the top and the page number is at the top left. No margin notes. Right edge of text is cut by the scan.

main_text.p: Ulterius quaeritur quatuor nonae batze-ni,quot numulis valeant?
Nunc 56 divido per 9 & proveniunt 6 numuli & 2/9 numuli.
main_text.head: De Additione Fractionum.
main_text.p: Superior dextra nota per inferiorem fi-nistram, ac inferior dextra per superiorem finistram multiplicatur, peracta multiplicatione, numeri adduntur, quo facto, De-nominator per alterum multiplicatur, & per multiplicatum, numerus per additio-nem collectus, dividitur: Et numerus qui in Divisione supra remanet, fit alterius fra-ctionis numerator: Divisor fit Denominator: Et cum producta fractione, si plures quam duae fuerint, fractio reliqua conjungitur: ut,

Primum dico ter 6 funt 18, quae seorsim scribo, ac progredior dicens: quater 5 funt 20, quae subscribo 18, & facta additione, proveniunt 38. Nunc Denominatorem per alterum multiplico, dicens: quater 6 funt 24, per quae divido triginta octo, & prove-nit[?]

page.notes: The scan is cut off at the right edge, so the last word of the page ("nit") is a fragment and the rest of the line is missing. Several fractions and the working in the equations were hard to read. "Hafficus" and the fractions "2/9", "5/6", "3/4", "3/5", "3/7" are doubtful. The first paragraph may continue from the previous page. The heading "De Additione Fractionum." is in italic and set as a sub-heading. The "Superior dextra" paragraph is a continuation of the sub-heading. Printed "Divifor" and "finiftram" use long s, which I have written as plain s. Digitiser marks and show-through were left out.
